{{Short description|Quantum analog of Bayes' theorem}}

In [[Quantum information science|quantum information theory]], a mix of [[quantum mechanics]] and [[information theory]], the '''Petz recovery map''' can be thought of a quantum analog of [[Bayes' theorem]]. Proposed by [[Dénes Petz]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Petz |first=Dénes |date=1986-03-01 |title=Sufficient subalgebras and the relative entropy of states of a von Neumann algebra |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-105/issue-1/Sufficient-subalgebras-and-the-relative-entropy-of-states-of-a/cmp/1104115260.pdf |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=105 |issue=1 |pages=123–131 |doi=10.1007/BF01212345 |bibcode=1986CMaPh.105..123P |s2cid=18836173 |issn=1432-0916}}</ref> the Petz recovery map is a [[quantum channel]] associated with a given quantum channel and [[quantum state]]. (A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) map.) This recovery map is designed in a manner that, when applied to an output state resulting from the given quantum channel acting on an input state, it enables the inference of the original input state. In essence, the Petz recovery map serves as a tool for reconstructing information about the initial quantum state from its transformed counterpart under the influence of the specified quantum channel.

The Petz recovery map finds applications in various domains, including [[quantum retrodiction]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Leifer |first1=M. S. |last2=Spekkens |first2=Robert W. |date=2013-11-27 |title=Towards a formulation of quantum theory as a causally neutral theory of Bayesian inference |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.88.052130 |journal=Physical Review A |volume=88 |issue=5 |article-number=052130 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.88.052130|bibcode=2013PhRvA..88e2130L |s2cid=43563970 |arxiv=1107.5849 }}</ref> [[quantum error correction]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Furuya |first1=Keiichiro |last2=Lashkari |first2=Nima |last3=Ouseph |first3=Shoy |date=2022-01-27 |title=Real-space RG, error correction and Petz map |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |language=en |volume=2022 |issue=1 |page=170 |doi=10.1007/JHEP01(2022)170 |bibcode=2022JHEP...01..170F |issn=1029-8479|doi-access=free |arxiv=2012.14001 }}</ref> and entanglement wedge reconstruction for black hole physics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Chi-Fang |last2=Penington |first2=Geoffrey |last3=Salton |first3=Grant |date=2020-01-28 |title=Entanglement wedge reconstruction using the Petz map |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |language=en |volume=2020 |issue=1 |page=168 |doi=10.1007/JHEP01(2020)168 |arxiv=1902.02844 |bibcode=2020JHEP...01..168C |issn=1029-8479}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cotler |first1=Jordan |last2=Hayden |first2=Patrick |last3=Penington |first3=Geoffrey |last4=Salton |first4=Grant |last5=Swingle |first5=Brian |last6=Walter |first6=Michael |date=2019-07-24 |title=Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction via Universal Recovery Channels |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevX.9.031011 |journal=Physical Review X |volume=9 |issue=3 |article-number=031011 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.9.031011|bibcode=2019PhRvX...9c1011C |arxiv=1704.05839 }}</ref>

== Definition ==
Suppose we have a quantum state which is described by a density operator <math>\sigma</math> and a quantum channel <math>\mathcal{E}</math>, the Petz recovery map is defined as<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Citation |last1=Khatri |first1=Sumeet |title=Principles of Quantum Communication Theory: A Modern Approach |date=2024-02-11 |arxiv=2011.04672 |last2=Wilde |first2=Mark M.}}</ref>

: <math>\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,\mathcal{E}}(\rho)=\sigma^{1/2}\mathcal{E}^{\dagger}(\mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-1/2}\rho  \mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-1/2})\sigma^{1/2}.</math>

Notice that <math>\mathcal{E}^{\dagger}</math> is the Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint of  <math>\mathcal{E}</math>. Then, we have that

: <math>\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,\mathcal{E}} (\mathcal{E}(\sigma))=\sigma.
</math>

Thus, the Petz recovery map perfectly recovers the state <math>\sigma</math> from the channel output <math>\mathcal{E}(\sigma).</math>

The Petz map has been generalized in various ways in the field of quantum information theory.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Universal recoverability in quantum information  |date=2016 |doi=10.1109/ISIT.2016.7541748 |s2cid=18189775 |last1=Junge |first1=Marius |last2=Renner |first2=Renato |last3=Sutter |first3=David |last4=Wilde |first4=Mark M. |last5=Winter |first5=Andreas |pages=2494–2498 |hdl=20.500.11850/120060 |isbn=978-1-5090-1806-2 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cree |first1=Sam |last2=Sorce |first2=Jonathan |date=2022-06-01 |title=Approximate Petz Recovery from the Geometry of Density Operators |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=392 |issue=3 |pages=907–919 |doi=10.1007/s00220-022-04357-2 |arxiv=2108.10893 |bibcode=2022CMaPh.392..907C |s2cid=237292763 |issn=1432-0916}}</ref>

== Properties of the Petz recovery map ==
A crucial property of the Petz recovery map is its ability to function as a quantum channel in certain cases, making it an essential tool in quantum information theory.

# The Petz recovery map is a [[completely positive map]], since (i) sandwiching by the positive semi-definite operator <math>\mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-1/2}(\cdot) \mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-1/2}</math> is completely positive; (ii) <math>\mathcal{E}^{\dagger}</math> is also completely positive when  <math>\mathcal{E}</math> is completely positive; and (iii) sandwiching by the positive semi-definite operator <math>\sigma^{1/2}(\cdot)\sigma^{1/2}</math> is completely positive. 
# It's also clear that  <math>\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,\mathcal{E}}</math> is trace non-increasing, since

<math>\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Tr}\left[\mathcal{P}_{\sigma, \mathcal{N}}(X)\right] & =\operatorname{Tr}\left[\sigma^{\frac{1}{2}} \mathcal{E}^{\dagger}\left(\mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}} X \mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) \sigma^{\frac{1}{2}}\right] \\
& =\operatorname{Tr}\left[\sigma \mathcal{E}^{\dagger}\left(\mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}} X \mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right] \\
& =\operatorname{Tr}\left[\mathcal{E}(\sigma) \mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}} X \mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right] \\
& =\operatorname{Tr}\left[\mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}} \mathcal{E}(\sigma) \mathcal{E}(\sigma)^{-\frac{1}{2}} X\right] \\
& =\operatorname{Tr}\left[\Pi_{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)} X\right] \\
& \leq \operatorname{Tr}[X]
\end{aligned}
</math>

From 1 and 2, when <math>\mathcal{E}(\sigma)
</math> is invertible, the Petz recovery map <math>\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,\mathcal{E}}</math> is a quantum channel, viz., a CPTP map.
